chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mukattib (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us, on the authority of his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, on the authority of Ali ibn Salim, on the authority of Abu Basir, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever recites 'Say: He, Allah is One' once, it is as if he has recited one third of the Qur'an, one third of the Torah, one third of the Gospel, and one third of the Psalms.

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He, Allah is One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas once?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq includes this narration in *al-Tawhid* to demonstrate that the concise declaration of divine unity in Surah Al-Ikhlas encapsulates the core essence of all previous revelations. By equating its reward to one-third of the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms, the Imam emphasizes that the concept of Tawhid is the unifying theological thread across all divine scriptures, with the remaining two-thirds of the Qur'an's reward derived from its detailed elaboration of this same principle.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 15. Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mukattib (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Abu `Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Musa ibn `Imran al-Nakha`I on the authority of his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali on the authority of `Ali ibn Salim on the authority of Abu Basir said Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said: “
Whoever recites the chapter: Say: He, Allah is One, once, it is as if he has recited one third of the Qur`an, one third of the Torah, one third of the Bible, and one third of the Psalms (of David).”
